notes: §1985:XIII.4.5.3 SR2: 'The availability of the phrases within the OPEN statement is dependent on the level of the Sequential I-O module supported by the implementation.' WiseOwl implements the level-2 Sequential I-O OPEN, so both RW OPEN phrases are available at --std 85: the grammar's openMode/openFileSpec take OUTPUT [WITH NO REWIND] and EXTEND (the double-barred level-2 element of §1985:VII.4.3.2), SequentialIoBinder#BindOpen binds them, CheckOpenModeForFile refuses INPUT/I-O on a report file (COBOL2371) and CheckOpenTapePhrase refuses NO REWIND with EXTEND (COBOL1803). Probes at --std 85: class e OUTPUT (FS=00, HELLO), OUTPUT WITH NO REWIND (FS=07, the 1985 non-reel status), OUTPUT then CLOSE then EXTEND (FS=00, two HELLO lines), EXTEND of a missing file (FS=35, the statement after it still runs), EXTEND of a missing OPTIONAL file (FS=05, file created); class b INPUT, I-O, INPUT REVERSED -> COBOL2371, EXTEND WITH NO REWIND -> COBOL1803, OPEN OUTPUT. -> COBOL0001; class c the 2002 SHARING phrase -> COBOL0900 and WITH LOCK -> COBOL5506. Classes a, d, f do not apply. The witness opens OUTPUT then EXTEND and prints DONE.

next.reason: 1985: "The availability of the phrases within the OPEN statement is dependent on the level of the Sequential I-O module supported"; 2023: "No module levels; the OPEN syntax rules (e.g. SR-14.9.27.3-1, -2) state no level dependency for phrase availability". 2023 has no module levels. The candidates cover OPEN phrases but none makes their availability depend on an implemented Sequential I-O level, so the 1985 requirement is dropped.
